description: ODC (EDITING coverage): touch a data model that THIS job did not create. The base is job:data-full-model, that is, the entities already exist when the first op runs - there is deliberately no spec op here, because creating and editing in the same job proves no editing at all. The target is the inherited WfCovProject, and the four changes are all on top of state that the OTHER job left written: add the attribute WfClosedOn to an entity that already had its 5 attributes, replace the Description that the other job wrote in Notes (and the Label that the platform had derived from the name), change the UpdateBehavior that nobody wrote by hand (the spec op inferred it as Optimized because of the Long Text) and create an EntityIndex over StartedOn, an INHERITED column. Outside the job that created them there are no aliases: entities are cited as 'IServerEntity:Name' and attributes by the path 'IServerEntity:Name/Attribute'. Each change has its get BEFORE and its get AFTER, and at the end the things this job did NOT touch (Name, the old index, the entity WfCovOrganization) are also read, to show that the edit was surgical and not a rebuild. The only new message of the job IS the result of change 3, and it is declared in expectedMessages: the platform re-evaluated the edited entity and asked again for Optimized because of the Long Text. It is this message, more than any get, that proves the change really entered the model.

expectedMessages.why: This is the point of change 3, not a defect: the inherited entity has a Long Text attribute (Notes, Text 2000000) and this job puts the UpdateBehavior back to Full, the platform default. The scalability suggestion only appears because Verify ran again over the entity AFTER the edit - in a job that only creates, this warning could never be born, because the spec op would already have put Optimized at birth and nobody would have contradicted it.

ops.name: WfCovProject
ops._why: (0) starting point: the entity ALREADY exists before the first op of this job. It comes from the base job:data-full-model, not from a spec here. The find also returns the 'WfCovProject Identifier' that the platform generated with it

(1) BEFORE, the entity: Attributes 5, Indexes 2, the Description written by the other job, and UpdateBehavior Optimized - which nobody asked for. The one who set it was the spec op, which makes every server entity be born Optimized when the job does not declare updateBehavior. Compare with get (13): WfCovOrganization, from the same base, was also born Optimized and was not touched

(2) BEFORE, the tree: the 5 attributes in birth order (Id, OrganizationId, Name, Notes, StartedOn), the TWO indexes - the AutoIndex_OrganizationId that the platform generates by itself for the FK and the UQ_WfCovProject_OrgName that the other job declared -, the SampleRecord with one IRecordAttributeValue per attribute and the entity actions. This is the snapshot that the dump (14) is compared against

(3) BEFORE, the attribute that will be edited: DataType Text with Length 2000000 (the translation of Long Text), IndexInParent 3, the Description written by the other job and Label 'Notes' - note that the Label is NOT empty: the platform always derives it from the name (StartedOn is born with Label 'Started On')
(4) BEFORE, the inherited column that the new index will cover: it exists, it is a Date, and no index touches it yet. This is where you see the derived Label 'Started On' mentioned in (3)
(5) BEFORE, the explicit index that already existed, over (OrganizationId, Name). It is the neighbor of the one that will be born, and in get (11) it must remain exactly the same

(6) BEFORE, who uses Notes: count 1, real 0 - only the value of the sample record (IRecordAttributeValue), which in ODC is a derived use. It serves to show in (8c) that changing Description and Label touches no consumer: author text is not a binding

ops.name: WfClosedOn
ops._why: (7a) CHANGE 1 - add an attribute to the inherited entity. The parent is not an $alias: aliases are local to the job that declares them, and the one who declared this entity was another job. Outside it the stable reference is 'IServerEntity:WfCovProject'

ops.value: Quando o projecto foi fechado. Acrescentado por edit-inherited-data.json, DEPOIS de a entidade existir.

ops._why: without this set the Label would be born derived from the name, 'Wf Closed On'; it is the same mechanism that gave 'Notes' and 'Started On' to the inherited attributes

(7b) AFTER: the new attribute, with the type, the Description and the Label that this job wrote. The alias $closed only exists because THIS job created it - it is the difference between what is inherited and what is added

ops.value: Notas do projecto. Description REESCRITA por edit-inherited-data.json: o texto anterior era o do job que criou a entidade.
ops._why: (8a) CHANGE 2 - Description and Label of an attribute that ALREADY EXISTED. I chose Notes and not Name or StartedOn on purpose: Notes is the only inherited attribute that already carried a Description written by an author, so here there really is a REPLACEMENT of text and not the filling of an empty field, which would prove much less

the Label was not empty either - it said 'Notes', derived from the name by the platform. Writing over it fixes it: from here on it is author text, and a future rename of the attribute no longer follows it (it is the same trap that rename-data-propagation.json shows)

(8b) AFTER: compare with get (3). The Description and the Label CHANGED; the DataType Text, the Length 2000000, the IsMandatory and the IndexInParent 3 STAYED - the attribute did not change place or type, only text
(8c) AFTER: exactly the list of (6), the same IRecordAttributeValue key. Description and Label are text, not a reference: no consumer was born or broke

(9a) CHANGE 3 - the UpdateBehavior of the entity. In the previous job nobody wrote it: it stayed Optimized because the spec op infers it from a Long Text attribute. Here the author puts it back to Full, over that inference - the case that only an editing job can show, because the value being swapped was not asked for by anyone, it was derived at birth. The platform answers with the scalability suggestion declared in expectedMessages

(9b) AFTER, the entity: compare with get (1). The UpdateBehavior CHANGED (Optimized -> Full) and Attributes went up from 5 to 6, which is change 1 showing up here too; EVERYTHING ELSE STAYED - Description, Label, Public False, ExposeReadOnly True. Indexes still says 2 because the new index is only born in the next op

ops.name: IX_WfCovProject_StartedOn
ops._why: (10a) CHANGE 4 - new index over an INHERITED column. The attribute is referenced by the path 'entity/attribute' and the kernel requires that it really belongs to the parent; the name follows the lane convention (IX_<Entity>_<Columns>), which already carries the Wf prefix through the entity name

(10b) AFTER: Unique false, Entity WfCovProject and Attributes with the inherited column. The index is new, the column is not - which is why this op could not exist in a job that creates everything from scratch
(11) WHAT REMAINED: the explicit index that already existed, identical to get (5), with the same AttributeKeys. Creating an index beside it does not rewrite the other one

(12) WHAT REMAINED: an inherited attribute that this job did not touch - Text, Length 120, mandatory, empty Description and Label still derived ('Name'). Put side by side with get (8b), it shows that the edit went TO the chosen attribute and not to the whole entity

(13) WHAT REMAINED: the other entity of the same base, intact - it keeps the UpdateBehavior Optimized with which the spec made it be born. It is the counter-proof of (9b): only WfCovProject, edited by this job, went to Full. It is also the proof that an editing job does not rebuild the model underneath - if there were a spec here, this reading would be worthless

(14) The final tree, to put beside the dump (2): WfClosedOn enters at the END of the attribute sequence and not in the middle, the 5 inherited ones keep the birth order, the SampleRecord gained by itself one more IRecordAttributeValue (5 -> 6) for the new column, and the indexes went from two to three - and the new one appears BETWEEN the other two, because indexes are not an author sequence. The entity actions are the same eight, with the same keys: adding a column does not re-create CreateOrUpdateWfCovProject. The dump lists them in another order, for the same reason - what the dump shows is the tree, and only the attributes have an order chosen by whoever writes
